you plan to rely on mods

Texts and dialog boxes are really small in 1440p screens. SFX and music with really low volume. Hard to manage controls for left-handed ppl.
I can't play properly, sry.

I played through this using steam family share. So first impressions.


Visuals are lovely with a clear amount of effort in love with each environment and sprite. Controls are a little spotting, but after a bit i got used to them.

Negatives
The dialogue. Specifically quest based dialogue. You can completely and accidentally miss vital information tied to a quest as the dialogue by default is automatic. This happened to me as i was attacked by an enemy, when i was told where to find a quest item. Perhaps a good way to counter this issue is a dialogue log for the player, or have the quest info update to display said info. 

I looked it up online and the location, just didn't exist in my world. Which means I was going to have to grind with no upgrades or anything. I'm not against a grind, but a grind caused by the seed not spawning a vital area that every guide online tells you to go???? ♥♥♥♥ that.

Got it back in 2018 and I just stumble up on the game again when I bought terraria. This game is trash and it tries to be a terraria clone with bugs and glitches and non fun features. Got my money back instantly since the devs don't need more money to screw up their game. Get terraria instead

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the starting hours lack sufficient tutorials or explanations for critical survival systems like hunger and farming.

citations.review_text:
Returned from 2018 to be reminded of why I just cannot like this game. Its beginning must be one of the worst ways to get into the game, where you blindly get into doing things without knowing critical things that matters. Such as HUNGER and how to just make some basic things for food and planting seeds. I'd have to look it all up online and that's just not how I want to play a game. I want the game to teach me that at the start, when it is also a very important thing to know about. 

Start is too vague from what would have been useful to know about. Shouldn't handhold players - unless they're new to gaming - but there's not even basic tutorials for the things that are important.

I don't enjoy this as much as terraria. In fact I couldn't even finish the tutorial quest. Its just too frustrating. I think I will move on to other things. What I disliked: combat, No mini-map (!!!), hunger system, Its quite sad, because I love sci-fi and I really wanted to like this.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the user interface feels tiny on modern displays and is described as clunky.

citations.review_text:
I kind of reccomend it, it looks nice, has a nice vibe, I don't know.
It's way too ambitious for its own good, the main questline is contrived and feels bolted onto the sandbox like why? ... to differentiate itself from terraria i guess.

download the fracking universe mod to have the best experience, and dont play the steam version use openstarbound because this game hasn't had support for years and the UI is tiny on modern displays.

The combat sucks just in general its not worth talking about. the exploration is good but the controls and UI are kind of clunky, lots of items and enemy variety but I dont know what this game is even trying to be. I think its a colony sim farming thing with space travel and more of a focus on agriculture and questing/crafting/sciencing then something like terraria which is more of a boss rush about leveling up your guy. I think starbound should of just dropped the combat in general and made it full on sciency community builder. There is no need for this game to have these linear scripted dungeons and boss fights and weapon upgrades. it just makes it boring in my opinion, starbound should of been more original and experimental in its design instead of trying to be like other games.

so this is my reccomendation: download fracking universe and play on casual mode so you dont need to deal with the pointless survival mechanics and item drop stuff, focus on farming and building new technology and build up a cool colony on a planet you like, avoid the main questline and combat as much as you can.

8/10 at its best. 2/10 for when its trying to be terraria or for some reason metroid (???)

oof, this one's a mess. hitboxes are totally off, like, how do you even miss that badly? the ui is just garbage, super clunky and ugly. story start is so dumb too, just really idiotic. and the character models? straight outta a cereal box, flat and lifeless. devs clearly just gave up on it, haven't seen any updates or anything to fix all this crap. it's just dead in the water. honestly, it just didn't grab me at all. really doesn't deserve all those "good" reviews it's somehow gotten. definitely skip this one.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the vanilla game as empty, unpolished, and lacking depth without mods.

citations.review_text: I like the game with mods, but I don't want to show any support for the devs and what they did. I'm playing it because I didn't know about the story behind the game, and I might as well play it now that I have it and have spent the money on it. I would not reccomend the game, though, as without mods it feels rather empty and hastily cobbled together. As stated above, though, it's good with mods. Only with mods.

Heavily flawed gem. 
It plays like an alt evolution of Terraria with a No Man's Sky coat of paint. However, the base game is chronically unpolished, and lacks both quality of life and depth. The entirety of the game feels like an abandoned first draft.

You can have fun with this game, but I HIGHLY recommend that you mod/workshop the OpenStarBound ver to make it more palatable and reduce the jank.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that space travel leaves the player with only the spacecraft as a permanent home, as planets do not offer a place to settle.

citations.review_text:
It's a great game. The issue is space travel, for me. There's never just one place to call home but the spacecraft. Maybe a space station. Even then, there's not exactly much to do but roleplay if not speedrun the main story. And roleplay requires friends or servers - I've never been on a server, so don't quote me on that.

And I get it; A space game is all about being in space. You're supposed to enjoy space.

If you're focused on the story like a majority of players, there's not much to enjoy about space. You go to a planet, research a few things you can find in one or two villages or buildings, go to a single destination to get some artifact and a new NPC at the sort of "hub" place, rinse and repeat until you defeat the bbeg.

You don't do side quests that help the main quest, because those genuinely give you trash - You use gear that the world gives to you from loot chests. Your inventory or ship storage becomes cluttered, and you don't sell anything because it's not really worth it when the environments give you more than enough to beat the game with.

There's nothing to do after beating the game, because you've beaten the game. Maybe you wrap up making a mech for yourself, even if it's the basic one. Maybe you get all upgrades and find all the secrets in the mission zones. Or you don't.

Mods CAN supplement these issues, and I think you should enter the game accepting that fact. Maybe give it a vanilla run first. Even then, most of what I've seen is just as unfortunately linear - Sorry mod makers, I love you but there's not enough to be done here.

It's fun, but it's obviously not Terraria 2.0, which a lot of people were hoping it would be initially. Just doesn't scratch that same itch. I would treat it more as a fun story game than a sandbox game like Terraria. The main issue is with all these planets you can explore, nowhere truly feels like home. You feel like a menace going from world to world sucking all the resources out of each planet and leaving them as wastelands.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the main storyline consists of repetitive fetch and scan quests paired with boss fights.

citations.review_text: it’s an interesting game. I really liked the progression system and the weapon system. The only issue is the repetition in the main storyline — like it keeps asking you to go scan an area, then fight a boss, then scan again, then fight another boss. So the missions feel kinda repetitive, but overall it’s still a good game.

In a universe of infinite procedurally generated fetch quests, why do I feel so alone?

The lore drops aspire to the level of second-rate fanfiction. The main storyline is stuck several levels below that, being both excruciatingly boring and poorly written (confusing 'reap' and 'wreak', etc.).

The appeal to this game for me was in the impression that you could create your own character and tell your own story. However, that promise is not realised. Progress is linear and exploration consists of the same few components in each category (weaponry, biomes, quests, dungeons, creatures, etc.) in various permutations. The game tells you you are exploring the vastness of space, but in effect you are walking round in circles. There is a dearth of original content and what is there is poorly designed and falls within a narrow and generally unpleasant aesthetic range. 

For designing characters and collecting 'their' gear, I'll stick with Terraria: there is no contest.

The community is strong, which is nice to see. Two themes emerge:

(1) The exploitation of interns in the development process of the game was regrettable.

(2) The game had a lot of potential that for various reasons not unrelated to (1) was never realised.

I am ignorant of (1) beyond the fact that it is an issue that is often brought up and lamented. It is something I wish I had been aware of prior to purchase.

I am unconvinced of (2). I think this game shows signs of being poorly planned from the get-go. I suspect the developers backed themselves into a corner with the reliance on procedural generation, which in the absence of a disciplined and creative planning process failed to produce diverse in-game experiences. 

Overall, it seems to me that this was always destined to be a game with a lot of Stuff in it and not much to say. 

Despite the above, this game might well be for you if you: really like guns and shoot-outs, find throwing bombs at people trying to shoot you thrilling, enj…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the soundtrack is a major highlight, with praise directed at Curtis's music.

citations.review_text:
I have mixed feelings about this game nowadays. I've grown up loving it, and still do have fun with it. Though, as I grow older, I come to realize the game's flaws (and they're pretty hard to ignore nowadays). 

The story is a heavily missed opportunity, the game could've been so much more impactful with a better story. Also, exploring the surface is usually a lot more fun and tends to give enough loot over the long run to make mining less important. There's also some features stuck into the game with no real reason to pay attention to them, such as fishing and fossil-collecting. While you can keep playing after the final boss, there's very little to motivate you to do so apart from the bounty hunter update tossed into the mix in update 1.4 (in my opinion, of course). 

That's all without addressing the major elephant in the room, of course. The thing that some people reading this review have been waiting for me to include. The fact that this game was built largely on unpaid labor is heartbreaking to me, and I couldn't really look at the game the same way again afterwards. 

However, since I put "recommended" in my review, you may be asking why given all the negative points I just listed. Because there are still a lot of good things about this game, that I think provide a pretty fun experience for at least 1 playthrough. Curtis's soundtrack is amazing, and in my opinion the game would've been forgotten way quicker if it weren't for the music (and it also could've gotten boring way faster). I love the variation in planets, biomes, villages, races, spacecrafts, overall just the diversity in life and cultures offered in the game. This isn't to say there's no room for improvement of course, but I would still consider it one of the game's strengths. I also like the variation in weapons and the dungeons (even though you can definitely see less effort put into the later dungeons of the main story). 

Overall, I would recommend this game for a fun survival-exploration exper…

One of my favorite sandbox games of all time!
The sound track is absolute bliss and this game is often the most relaxing experience out there. ><
A brief history of the game and it's development certainly has some skeletons in it's closet due to how community contributions were treated, but the games 10 years old and an absolute classic!
Just enjoy it <3

beautiful visuals and music, but the game is sorely lacking in actual content and game systems which not even mods can rectify. I could write an essay on the problematic and slow development of this game as someone who has been playing since ~2014, but that's already been done to death in various youtube videos, so instead I'll just say that a lot of the work on this game was by unpaid and underage programmers. I wish all the best to the programmers and to curtis, but please do not buy this game

It's just flippin' awesome. The pixel art is beautiful and well put-together. The Soundtrack is still at 100% volume after hundreds of hours. The exploration of new planets is fun, though ofc you'll eventually have seen all the different kinds of buildings. The story... I mean, who plays Sandbox games for the Story? xd It's totally good enough for this kind of game. 
Playing with friends makes this naturally much better ofc. Grab a friend and give it a try! 
The workshop-integration (plus off-steam mods) make this game even better! People really love this game for a reason! 
10/10, would traverse star-bound again! 🚀

It's a decently fun and beautiful game. Fantastic soundtrack! All of it's basic gameplay is decent.

The entire time I've played through this story, I was waiting for something INTERESTING to happen... Like a plot twist, something crazy, something exciting. That never happens.

There's nothing exciting or interesting about the story itself. It would be better if it didn't exist, I don't care about any of the NPC friends you make in the story, I don't even care about that crippled old woman, practically all she does is just sit there and tell me to go scan things. The most interesting characters to me are the penguins, and they aren't even the ones that give you lots of dialogue.

The bosses are fun for the most part, but don't expect anything that's going to knock your socks off.

All in all, I love this game. But the story is horribly boring.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a modding community on the Steam Workshop, with content ranging from quality-of-life additions to total conversion overhaul mods like Frackin' Universe.

citations.review_text: I basically only play it for some mods and to build cool stuff, except dont play Frackin Universe that ♥♥♥♥ is stinky and is just a bootleg wannabe gregtech modpack for mc. If you like to build its a fine game, but don't go into this expecting some indepth exploration or meaningful progression (i literally mod out the story lol), its just not got the bones for that due to the disastrous development it went through.
I love this game, you can do soooo much and there is alot in the workshop. People have much imagination and ideas for this game...

At its core, it's a huge sandbox full of planets to explore, creatures to discover, bases to build, and secrets to uncover. There is always something to do, whether you're progressing through the story, decorating your ship, collecting rare items, or simply wandering off to see what strange world you might find next.

The main story itself is pretty neat. It provides enough structure to guide you through the game without taking away the freedom that makes Starbound so enjoyable. I always appreciated how it encouraged exploration rather than forcing you down a strict path. Combined with the variety of biomes, races, and equipment, the game constantly rewards curiosity.

Starbound is also fantastic with friends. Exploring the galaxy together, building colonies, tackling bosses, or just messing around on random planets leads to countless memorable moments. Some of my favorite experiences came from multiplayer sessions where we started with a simple goal and somehow ended up spending hours doing something completely different. 

As much as I love the base game, the real magic of Starbound lies in its modding scene. The Steam Workshop support is excellent, and the community has created an incredible amount of content. Entire gameplay systems, new races, additional planets, and quality-of-life improvements breathe even more life into the game.

And then there are the overhaul mods. Projects like Frackin' Universe practically transform Starbound into a completely new experience. New stories, mechanics, crafting systems, and progression paths add hundreds of hours of content and make revisiting the game feel fresh all over again. Few games benefit from modding as much as Starbound does.

Starbound may not be perfect, and some people prefer Terraria's faster pace, but for me there is something special about the sense of adventure it creates. Between the endless exploration, enjoyable story, great co-op, and one of the best modding communities around, it remains one of the ga…

I'd say it's a really good game, but base game is very imperfect, and every single person who plays it agrees with that sentiment. I really love the game personally, it has it's charm, and while yes it's not exactly game of the year, or as good as games like Terraria, are you really coming to this *space* game for a Terraria like experience? I've played both, and frankly I find myself playing Starbound more thanks to it's open ended-ness, but that is all because of personal taste, and i love the creativity it invokes in me when building Colony settlements. 

However, I really wish the game got more polished before release, like I would never play Vanilla Starbound ever again after experiencing all the mods the game has to offer than improve the experience majorly. If you play this game, I recommend playing base game before modding, but if you must it is good to get performance mods first due to the frequent lag problems this game would give me on my old laptop.

The game really shines at it's brightest with friends, that's the whole reason I first got, and started plaything this game to begin with, but really however you play this game is on you, and how you personally have fun (or don't) with it.

I'm late to this game and I wish I would've discovered it sooner. I played through the entire game vanilla before I modded, and honest review on both: 
Vanilla, it's good, I know some people feel it's unfinished, but as someone who doesn't know the history behind the game outside of the game itself it feels like a completed game and it has good flow/pacing. You can continue to explore after you complete the full storyline which is really nice, especially for builders. 
Modded: It feels like modded minecraft and terraria had a kid. I'm doing Frackin' and because I'm so late to the ballgame it's not buggy (love this) and there's very few things missing. I love the mod commitment to the love of the game, there's so much in depth lore, but there is also SOOOO much to do. I love building and the addition of all the cool races and their furniture and planets and such, and that there was some extended stuff onto the base game stories. Really nice to bring life into the game after you've done all you felt you could do in vanilla. 
I'd recommend this game for sure, and I hope that they keep it alive.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the main story and quests as repetitive, noting that planet exploration involves scanning objects and completing endless fetch or kill tasks.

citations.review_text:
The game loop is not bad at all, but very repetitive. The different worlds are well generated, but not very unique from each other. The main storyline, the peacekeeper questline, and the quests given by npcs, are pretty decent in a vacuum, but get repetitive pretty fast. The combat is not the best, but mech combat is pretty enjoyable - especially after some upgrades. 

Overall, the main story is pretty decent (not groundbreaking in any way, but not bad either), but surprisingly enough, for being a survival sandbox, the game lacks replayability after the first playthrough. Also the achievements are torture.

Starbound. What to say that hasn't already been said? I did have fun with the game, I liked the linear story missions, I liked the bosses, I loved some of the mechanics like turning into a ball that can roll on the ceiling, I liked stuffing my ship with various decorations and junk. But, there always something that brought down the experience just a little bit. Many of the story "missions" being to explore random planets and get lucky that you find the things you need to scan. The fact that it feels really unoptimized and held together by hopes. The limitless fetch/kill quests with mixed rewards. Way back when the Bounty Hunter/Mech update dropped I naively thought that Starbound would start making updates that would slowly bring it to prominence. Yeah, that didn't happen and it is such a shame that it will never happen. Regardless, I can't bring myself to say that I would not recommend this game. I still think about some of the mechanics, I still think about the Matter Manipulator, I still think about the concept of the plot and its loose ends. All together, a decent game that had potential and one that people can get at least some enjoyment out of.

The game is repetitive with scanning objects from different planets and going into an instance for the entire game. It's last update was back in 2019 and there has been silence after it,

i would leave a positive review on this game but the modders put more love into this game compared to Chucklefish.

You're better off playing Terraria.

Played this game for YEARS and I can safely say its only remotely fun if modded.

The quests are extremely tedious and fetchy, the same formula over and over again.

None of the major npcs are very memorable except maybe Nuru and that old woman I cant remember the name of.

Every single mechanic and aspect of this game feels half-baked and unfinished which actually makes sense if you know the history behind this game. (look it up)

Oh, Starbound... My relationship with this game is complicated. I remember when it was in early access and seemed full of potential. So many features seemed fascinating and interesting - some planets didn't have molten cores, but freezing temperatures. 
I don't know what happend. They removed several of the most promising features in favor of more bland exploration with less to do. All planets of a type feel the same, putting aside the occasional copypasted in settlement. Most quests are randomly generated filler with rewards that are rarely worth it. The main quest is now a fairly generic storyline. And overall, the game just doesn't feel finished.

I've given this game a shot over and over again. I've played it through multiple times with friends. I've played it modded. And there IS stuff to love here. I love the distinct identities they gave to many of the races, there are some genuinely fun systems. But it ultimately all feels shallow. I simply cannot, in good conscience, recommend this game at this point because of that.

If you decide that you want to give this game a shot despite all that, and see what it has to offer, I recommend the frackin universe mod. Find Svetlana's secret place and jam out to the music (or just look up "Starbound Svetlana" on Youtube, it's a remix of Secret of Mana's A Curious Tale), and crucially, play it with friends. More power to you if you decide to take this route.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the developers abandoned the game years ago without updates, only to later release a 10th-anniversary vinyl soundtrack.

citations.review_text:
Great game, but the company decided that one of it's potential best sellers was abandonware material instead. Then they go and release a vinyl for their "10th anniversary" even though they've done *nothing* for this game in years. If they decided to update this game with some major updates I'll change my review to a thumbs up, but I know that won't happen. This game was such a huge part of growing up, and it's sad that the company abandoned this title and then desperately clawing for more money from us by trying to sell us vinyl, which will inevitably get people buying into their garbage again. 

On to another point, this company decided they didn't need to pay underaged volunteers to log hundreds of hours of coding, writing, and design work on Starbound whilst the company leadership profited off of it. Their response to this was also dumb, as they stated that they had no formal obligation to work specific hours or to meet any strict deadlines, which I'm sure we all understand is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ when it comes to the gaming industry. It's just another clear cut case of corporate greed and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ people owning great game titles. There's a reason Stardew Valley's creator Eric Barone publicly announced that he developed Stardew Valley entirely alone and moved the game to self-publishing to distance himself from the issues that Chucklefish has. I also need to state that Finn Brice did indeed decide to berate and yell at Clark Powell when his business ethics were questioned.

On to the Kickstarter now, this game was over-hyped, promising a deep procedural sandbox universe, with many options from back then not currently existing in today's version of the game. On its early launches, it was an underdeveloped "tech demo" which was missing foundational features as advertised on the Kickstarter. It also now is missing features from earlier versions of the game's lifespan as well, like fully randomized monsters, a lot of the old lore being completely scrapped, changing the story to be…

Well, I *almost* forgot I’d bought this game—much like the developers seem to have forgotten to give it the bug fixes it deserves before abandoning it for years. Thanks to the 10th-anniversary vinyl release, I was reminded that maybe it’s finally time to give this a “Not Recommended.”

I love *Terraria*, and I really wanted *Starbound* to succeed as well. Unfortunately, the vanilla game feels far too shallow, and the developers’ refusal to provide even basic bug fixes or quality-of-life updates—while continuing to squeeze whatever value remains from the IP—leaves a bad taste in my mouth.

For those who haven’t stumbled across this game before: lucky you. Spend your time and money on something else. After all these years, there are much better alternatives than this abandoned project.

Not the developers trying to come back with a single piece of 10th anniversary merchandise after radio silence for several years, lmfao.

They legit left this game unfinished with their tails between their legs. And not just because they ran out of funds, mind you, but because they had their unpaid labor exposed. 

The real kicker is if they DO decide to update the game for its 10th anniversary, that's actually a detriment to us. Why? Because the game was left abandoned for so long that the scene is basically 90% mods and 10% base game at this point. A minor tweak to the source code will break a LOT of peoples' ♥♥♥♥. That's embarrassing. 

And Hell if we're going this far dogging on the game, the state this thing is in is SO ANNOYING. Literally 95% of my deaths were from being swarmed by a small army of monsters just for being in their general vicinity, unable to kill all of them before they killed me or gave me a breath to heal. WHY DO THEY ALL MOVE SO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FAST. All I want is one deathless run, starting over and over and over again because of annoying ass intentional game design blows chunks. At least in Minecraft, I have to REALLY mess up to get cornered by six zombies, two skeletons, and a spider. In Starbound, you can just dig your way into a mess of them. Or walk away and come back and sixteen tiny flying creatures have spawned where you stood. And whose idea was the stupid invincible ghost that stops you from taking too much fuel from moons? How is that fun game design when it homes in on you increasingly fast, can phase through the moon, is invulnerable, and kills you in one hit? AND YOU CAN JUST BUY FUEL AT THE OUTPOST? And oh, boy, do I love accidentally coming across a settlement of hostile NPCs who gun me down without even trying!

I'd like a game that follows up on what the beta promised. Maybe, someday, that'll happen. After all, the source code to this game was even so poorly guarded that it's been leaked multiple times.
Developers abandoned this game for years and then, as if nothing had happened, droped a vinyl release for 10th anniversary. They take us for dumb fools or what..

Game is basically abandoned by the developers after having got their money, 13+ years of a game that had potential to be next Terraria, only to massacred during its development and left to rot, only reason this game is still alive and thriving is because of the dedicated Modders. Now after that long time the devs come back with a Anniversary Vynil that is just a spit in the face to their last fans that still dwell on this game, trying to make a quick checkout as their funds run low.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the procedurally generated planets as repetitive and lacking in unique identity after exploring the initial worlds.

citations.review_text:
I got this game when it very first dropped on Steam, and I played the heck out of it, even though the content was pretty lacking at the time. However, in each iteration of content updates, the game has only become worse and worse. While they have done a fairly good job of making the worlds feel a bit more alive and interesting, the procedurally generated planets you explore and land on become boring copies of each other after just one or two worlds. I like that the game has a long story sequence to get things started, but eventually after reaching the space station, you are given a bunch of incredibly vague quests, including ones that are wayyyy too high level for you. Maybe they just did a terrible job at scaling the play for single players? It honestly feels like a lot of the boss battles and random fights are assuming you have friends with you to help, but without those other players, the difficulty is insane. I found myself dying over and over and over and over again. Sometimes in places that made no sense to even have difficult enemies. 

I eventually just gave up even trying to play. It suffers from the same issue as No Man's Sky. You can fluff up the procedurally generated worlds with all the content and pre-built dungeons or towns you want, but at the end of the day, the worlds just feel the same and boring. At least with Terraria, the world stays the same through the entire playthrough. You get to learn the areas above and below ground and make it your home over time. This game feels more like a chore to land on a planet, collect a few resources you have to get, then leave the planet, never to return again. There is no inventive to build on any particular planet. In fact, it's way better to just put your crafting stuff on your ship and never build at all. 

TLDR: Game is extremely boring very quickly, but also you will die a million times to the easiest monsters. Just not that fun.

First played in Early Access, when it was a lot of fun. Planets where randomly generated as well as the creatures roaming them. Every planet was a bit different and much fun to explore.

With the release of 1.0 it lost most of the things that made it fun in the first place. A very short story was added, planets randomnes (and fun) were reduced to a handfull of the same old variations of planets, with just a few prebuild creatures and dungeons to find there.

Had a lot of fun in the early versions of early access, but the replayability and the fun went aways with the release of the "full" game. [u]Not recommended.[/u]

Perfectly Generic Game.

I really tried to like this game... I have way over 2000 hours despite what's shown in my profile since I spent an ungodly amount of time creating mods from custom races to QoL features for it and it doesn't track your playtime if you play from a modding folder separate from the steam install, this was long before the publishers were outed as not-so-nice people. In the end it was for nothing because it's impossible to salvage such a bare bones game, it commits the same sin as Elite Dangerous and No Mans Sky where you're given near infinite stars to explore but the content is so shallow that you'll basically see everything within a few hours. There's boss fights which are ridiculously basic and boring, and progression is locked behind a dumb story. Combat mechanics are close to nonexistent, weapons are generic pokey pokey swords/sticks or small/big pew pews with no variety to them and their randomized nature makes it so it's impossible to find anything useful.
The best way to play this game is in a creative mode, ignoring every single mechanic but construction because it seems like it's the only actually well designed system in the game, and making cute scenes, or maybe RP with your furry friends, if you have any.

Oh, Starbound... My relationship with this game is complicated. I remember when it was in early access and seemed full of potential. So many features seemed fascinating and interesting - some planets didn't have molten cores, but freezing temperatures. 
I don't know what happend. They removed several of the most promising features in favor of more bland exploration with less to do. All planets of a type feel the same, putting aside the occasional copypasted in settlement. Most quests are randomly generated filler with rewards that are rarely worth it. The main quest is now a fairly generic storyline. And overall, the game just doesn't feel finished.

I've given this game a shot over and over again. I've played it through multiple times with friends. I've played it modded. And there IS stuff to love here. I love the distinct identities they gave to many of the races, there are some genuinely fun systems. But it ultimately all feels shallow. I simply cannot, in good conscience, recommend this game at this point because of that.

If you decide that you want to give this game a shot despite all that, and see what it has to offer, I recommend the frackin universe mod. Find Svetlana's secret place and jam out to the music (or just look up "Starbound Svetlana" on Youtube, it's a remix of Secret of Mana's A Curious Tale), and crucially, play it with friends. More power to you if you decide to take this route.

Man I love this ♥♥♥♥ ass, ♥♥♥♥ ass game. It sucks. Multiplayer is so unreliable that this game can be considered psychological horror. The building, and crafting, is slow as hell, both modded and unmodded. The inventory system is terrible. The development process was terrible, look it up. Most of the mods are no longer being updated. But despite this, I still get this itch sometimes. To boot it up with my friend, and pray that our game doesn't crash.

Boring and unfinished. Planets feel inconsequential and the shoe horned narrative grinds the pace down to a halt. 

Boss fights are DPS checks with finicky attack patterns that you can't quite dodge accurately. Enemies are quite basic (melee, ranged only). 

View port is too constricted by default. Wish the zoom feature worked further out without lagging my device.

I'm inclined to believe the memory links are real. Have crashed and lagged (in single player) over longer playthroughs a few times unexpectedly.

Modding is a life line (frackin universe especially), but the skeleton of this game is very hollow. Underpaid artist controversy doesn't help.

I'd say it's a really good game, but base game is very imperfect, and every single person who plays it agrees with that sentiment. I really love the game personally, it has it's charm, and while yes it's not exactly game of the year, or as good as games like Terraria, are you really coming to this *space* game for a Terraria like experience? I've played both, and frankly I find myself playing Starbound more thanks to it's open ended-ness, but that is all because of personal taste, and i love the creativity it invokes in me when building Colony settlements. 

However, I really wish the game got more polished before release, like I would never play Vanilla Starbound ever again after experiencing all the mods the game has to offer than improve the experience majorly. If you play this game, I recommend playing base game before modding, but if you must it is good to get performance mods first due to the frequent lag problems this game would give me on my old laptop.

The game really shines at it's brightest with friends, that's the whole reason I first got, and started plaything this game to begin with, but really however you play this game is on you, and how you personally have fun (or don't) with it.

citations.review_text:
I got this game when it very first dropped on Steam, and I played the heck out of it, even though the content was pretty lacking at the time. However, in each iteration of content updates, the game has only become worse and worse. While they have done a fairly good job of making the worlds feel a bit more alive and interesting, the procedurally generated planets you explore and land on become boring copies of each other after just one or two worlds. I like that the game has a long story sequence to get things started, but eventually after reaching the space station, you are given a bunch of incredibly vague quests, including ones that are wayyyy too high level for you. Maybe they just did a terrible job at scaling the play for single players? It honestly feels like a lot of the boss battles and random fights are assuming you have friends with you to help, but without those other players, the difficulty is insane. I found myself dying over and over and over and over again. Sometimes in places that made no sense to even have difficult enemies. 

I eventually just gave up even trying to play. It suffers from the same issue as No Man's Sky. You can fluff up the procedurally generated worlds with all the content and pre-built dungeons or towns you want, but at the end of the day, the worlds just feel the same and boring. At least with Terraria, the world stays the same through the entire playthrough. You get to learn the areas above and below ground and make it your home over time. This game feels more like a chore to land on a planet, collect a few resources you have to get, then leave the planet, never to return again. There is no inventive to build on any particular planet. In fact, it's way better to just put your crafting stuff on your ship and never build at all. 

TLDR: Game is extremely boring very quickly, but also you will die a million times to the easiest monsters. Just not that fun.

Not the developers trying to come back with a single piece of 10th anniversary merchandise after radio silence for several years, lmfao.

They legit left this game unfinished with their tails between their legs. And not just because they ran out of funds, mind you, but because they had their unpaid labor exposed. 

The real kicker is if they DO decide to update the game for its 10th anniversary, that's actually a detriment to us. Why? Because the game was left abandoned for so long that the scene is basically 90% mods and 10% base game at this point. A minor tweak to the source code will break a LOT of peoples' ♥♥♥♥. That's embarrassing. 

And Hell if we're going this far dogging on the game, the state this thing is in is SO ANNOYING. Literally 95% of my deaths were from being swarmed by a small army of monsters just for being in their general vicinity, unable to kill all of them before they killed me or gave me a breath to heal. WHY DO THEY ALL MOVE SO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FAST. All I want is one deathless run, starting over and over and over again because of annoying ass intentional game design blows chunks. At least in Minecraft, I have to REALLY mess up to get cornered by six zombies, two skeletons, and a spider. In Starbound, you can just dig your way into a mess of them. Or walk away and come back and sixteen tiny flying creatures have spawned where you stood. And whose idea was the stupid invincible ghost that stops you from taking too much fuel from moons? How is that fun game design when it homes in on you increasingly fast, can phase through the moon, is invulnerable, and kills you in one hit? AND YOU CAN JUST BUY FUEL AT THE OUTPOST? And oh, boy, do I love accidentally coming across a settlement of hostile NPCs who gun me down without even trying!

I'd like a game that follows up on what the beta promised. Maybe, someday, that'll happen. After all, the source code to this game was even so poorly guarded that it's been leaked multiple times.
